title: Beyond the bill count: State AI legislative maturity atlas
scope: Representative legislative anchors across all 50 states; District of Columbia separate. Not an exhaustive legal inventory or state ranking. Empty domain cells mean not assessed in the selected corpus.

states.name: Alabama
states.claim: Deceptive election media: disclosure and remedies in the enrolled measure.
states.boundary: Enactment cross-checked against NCSL; enrolled text alone is not proof of signature.

states.name: Alaska
states.claim: Budget legislation includes state AI planning and project provisions.
states.boundary: Official history confirms enactment; AI scope is identified by NCSL. Spending and delivery were not audited.

states.name: Arizona
states.claim: Medical-necessity denials require independent medical-director review rather than sole reliance on recommendations.
states.boundary: A technology-neutral insurance safeguard; applies from July 1, 2026. Not a general AI law.

states.name: Arkansas
states.claim: Allocates specified ownership interests associated with AI output and training, including employment circumstances.
states.boundary: State-law allocation does not establish federal copyright eligibility or eliminate existing rights.

states.name: California
states.claim: Frontier-model risk frameworks and incident reporting; a separate companion-chatbot law addresses disclosure and user safeguards.
states.boundary: Different laws, covered entities and thresholds. An official reporting portal is an implementation artifact, not demonstrated risk reduction.
states.implementation: public artifact observed; effectiveness not assessed

states.name: Colorado
states.claim: The replacement automated-decision framework assigns documentation, notice, correction and meaningful human-review duties.
states.boundary: Core requirements begin January 1, 2027. The earlier SB24-205 regime is not the current implementation baseline.

states.name: Connecticut
states.claim: Annual state-agency AI inventory and ongoing assessment duties.
states.boundary: This entry assesses the 2023 public-sector mechanism. The complete effect of PA26-15 is outside this edition's assessed corpus.
states.implementation: public artifact observed; effectiveness not assessed

states.name: Delaware
states.claim: Creates an AI commission with inventory and recommendation responsibilities.
states.boundary: A legislative institution is not proof that private-sector controls or recommendations have been implemented.

states.name: Florida
states.claim: Requires disclaimers for covered political advertising using generated media.
states.boundary: Election-specific scope and statutory intent conditions; effective July 1, 2024.

states.name: Georgia
states.claim: Signed legislation addresses conversational AI interactions with minors and crisis-resource access.
states.boundary: Official Senate signing account supports this narrow description; provision-level effective dates were not independently resolved here.

states.name: Hawaii
states.claim: Addresses materially deceptive campaign media with disclosure exceptions.
states.boundary: Election-period and media-format conditions matter; not a general synthetic-content prohibition.

states.name: Idaho
states.claim: The FAIR Elections Act addresses deceptive generated election media.
states.boundary: Secondary-source verification only: the legislature's website was inaccessible to this review. Not included in primary-only comparisons.

states.name: Illinois
states.claim: Extends employment civil-rights protections to discriminatory AI use and requires notice.
states.boundary: Effective January 1, 2026. Rulemaking and employer compliance were not audited.

states.name: Indiana
states.claim: Creates public AI governance arrangements, including standards for voluntary public-entity inventories.
states.boundary: The inventory submission provision is permissive. Its July 1, 2025 start does not make all inventories mandatory.

states.name: Iowa
states.claim: Addresses dissemination of altered explicit depictions as harassment.
states.boundary: A targeted likeness safeguard; not a general model-development or deployment framework.

states.name: Kansas
states.claim: Signed legislation addresses AI-generated sexual depictions and related privacy harms.
states.boundary: Offense-specific scope; enactment does not establish implementation or enforcement outcomes.

states.name: Kentucky
states.claim: Extends protections concerning sexual depictions of minors to specified computer-generated material.
states.boundary: This selected criminal-law anchor does not represent Kentucky's full privacy or AI portfolio.

states.name: Louisiana
states.claim: Addresses nonconsensual AI-generated nude images.
states.boundary: The selected offense has particular knowledge, consent and depiction elements; no general AI maturity score is inferred.

states.name: Maine
states.claim: Requires disclosures for consumer-facing chatbots where users could be misled into believing they are interacting with a human.
states.boundary: A consumer transparency mechanism, not a general audit or risk-management obligation.

states.name: Maryland
states.claim: Directs public-sector AI inventories, policies and assessment arrangements.
states.boundary: Applies to state governance; this record does not characterize Maryland's separate consumer privacy regime.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.claim: Extends protections against image-based abuse; state guidance addresses student deepfake incidents.
states.boundary: The selected legislation and 2026 school guidance are distinct evidence objects; guidance is not evidence of universal school compliance.
states.implementation: public artifact observed; effectiveness not assessed

states.name: Michigan
states.claim: Regulates specified deceptive election media, as explained in the Attorney General's 2026 voter-protection guidance.
states.boundary: Campaign context, timing and statutory exceptions limit applicability.

states.name: Minnesota
states.claim: Provides covered consumers with profiling-related rights, including information and review-related protections.
states.boundary: Consumer privacy thresholds and exemptions apply. This is not a universal right governing every AI decision.

states.name: Mississippi
states.claim: Addresses deceptive election digitizations within a specified pre-election window.
states.boundary: Effective July 1, 2024; this entry uses the legislature's enacted-bill summary.

states.name: Missouri
states.claim: The official record shows a committee do-pass status for an AI online-content proposal.
states.boundary: No enactment is established for this instrument. The displayed prospective effective date is not evidence that it became law.

states.name: Montana
states.claim: Combines computing protections with risk-management provisions for AI controlling critical infrastructure.
states.boundary: Narrow infrastructure trigger. The final law should not be described as containing the proposal's discarded shutdown requirement.

states.name: Nebraska
states.claim: Requires data-protection assessments for covered high-risk processing, including specified profiling.
states.boundary: A consumer privacy mechanism with thresholds and exemptions, not an AI-only statute.

states.name: Nevada
states.claim: Restricts licensed mental- and behavioral-health providers' use of AI to deliver direct care, with administrative exceptions.
states.boundary: A professional-care boundary; does not prohibit every AI use in health services.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.claim: Addresses state-government AI use, transparency and human oversight.
states.boundary: Public-sector scope; it should not be presented as a private-sector omnibus regime.

states.name: New Jersey
states.claim: Creates targeted civil and criminal protections involving deceptive generated media.
states.boundary: Specific injury, conduct and intent elements matter; publication of synthetic media is not uniformly unlawful.

states.name: New Mexico
states.claim: Adds campaign disclosure requirements for covered AI-generated media.
states.boundary: Election safeguards do not establish general AI-provider accountability duties.

states.name: New York
states.claim: The amended RAISE framework addresses frontier-model safety and regulatory accountability.
states.boundary: Effective January 1, 2027. The 2026 amendment controls this edition's date treatment.

states.name: North Carolina
states.claim: Existing law covers specified AI-generated private images and sexual-exploitation material.
states.boundary: The cited legislative analysis describes existing law separately from H934's proposed changes; only its current-law discussion supports this entry.

states.name: North Dakota
states.claim: Requires identification of covered AI impersonation in political communications.
states.boundary: Campaign-specific trigger. Routine text assistance should not be conflated with covered impersonation.

states.name: Ohio
states.claim: Requires a state model AI policy and school-system adoption of AI-use policies by July 1, 2026.
states.boundary: The model policy is publicly available; local adoption and policy effectiveness were not audited.
states.implementation: public artifact observed; effectiveness not assessed

states.name: Oklahoma
states.claim: Signed legislation extends protections against nonconsensual intimate imagery to AI-generated material.
states.boundary: Targeted criminal-law protection; not evidence of a comprehensive AI accountability system.

states.name: Oregon
states.claim: Restricts nonhuman AI use of protected nursing titles.
states.boundary: A professional-title rule. The cited code edition does not incorporate all 2026 session changes.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.claim: Updates child-sexual-abuse depiction provisions to address specified synthetic material.
states.boundary: The selected criminal statute is not a full account of state AI legislation or administrative use.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.instrument: §6-48.1-7, Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act
states.claim: Requires assessments for covered high-risk processing, including specified profiling.
states.boundary: Effective January 1, 2026; consumer-data scope and exemptions apply.

states.name: South Carolina
states.claim: Signed legislation addresses unauthorized intimate-image disclosure, including AI-generated depictions.
states.boundary: May 12, 2025 signature and May 29 ceremonial event are distinct dates.

states.name: South Dakota
states.claim: Extends child-sexual-abuse material definitions to specified AI-generated depictions.
states.boundary: Depiction and offense elements constrain scope; not a general ban on generative AI.

states.name: Tennessee
states.claim: Protects voice and likeness interests against specified AI-related misuse.
states.boundary: Publicity and likeness rights operate differently from model-safety regulation.

states.name: Texas
states.claim: Sets prohibited uses, specified disclosure duties and an enforcement and sandbox structure.
states.boundary: Effective January 1, 2026. The enacted discrimination standard is intentional conduct, not a general disparate-impact test.

states.name: Utah
states.instrument: AI Policy Act and subsequent amendments
states.claim: An AI policy office and regulatory-mitigation program coexist with disclosure and mental-health chatbot safeguards.
states.boundary: The office describes a bounded prescription-renewal pilot. Agency-reported operation is not independent validation of clinical safety.
states.implementation: agency reports bounded program operation; outcomes not independently assessed

states.name: Vermont
states.claim: Assigns public AI review, inventory and reporting responsibilities to a state division.
states.boundary: Institutional duties are assessed here; performance of every mandated review is not established.

states.name: Virginia
states.claim: Gives covered consumers profiling opt-out rights and an appeal process for rights requests.
states.boundary: Consumer privacy coverage and exemptions apply; this is not an omnibus AI-specific assessment.

states.name: Washington
states.claim: Enacts a companion-chatbot regulatory framework.
states.boundary: Signed March 24, 2026; effective January 1, 2027. Enacted and effective are visibly separated in this atlas.

states.name: West Virginia
states.claim: Establishes a state AI task force and governance responsibilities.
states.boundary: This institutional anchor does not imply that every recommendation has become a binding rule.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.claim: Requires AI disclosures in covered political advertising.
states.boundary: Official Ethics Commission implementation material; effective March 23, 2024. The review does not assess enforcement outcomes.
states.implementation: public artifact observed; effectiveness not assessed

states.name: Wyoming
states.claim: Addresses AI-enabled harms involving minors, with specified criminal and developer-liability provisions.
states.boundary: Effective July 1, 2026. Particular knowledge and intent conditions matter.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.instrument: No anchor classified in this edition
states.claim: Included separately from the 50 states; legislative classification remains unassessed.
states.boundary: This is a research gap, not a finding that the District has no applicable law.
